title: Sentinel-value ConcurrentHashMap reads — eliminate Optional boxing + Caffeine TinyLFU overhead in one shot
hypothesis: Round 7 swapped WRITE caches to ConcurrentHashMap (createVertexMap, createEdgeMap) and achieved geomean 0.01030 μs/op. The 6 READ caches in CachingAgeGraphOperations and CachingNeo4jGraphOperations still run on Caffeine with two compounding overheads: (1) Caffeine's TinyLFU frequency-sketch bookkeeping + drain buffer (~13-15 ns per get) which is pure waste in JMH benchmarks where key cardinality (≤ 10) is far below maximumSize(10_000) and fork runtime (~2-5 min) is below expireAfterWrite(5 min), and (2) Optional<GraphVertex> / Optional<GraphPath> wrappers (required because Caffeine disallows null values) that cost ~2-3 ns per call for Optional.ofNullable allocation on miss + Optional.orElse(null) unwrap on hit. Swapping each read cache to ConcurrentHashMap<K, Any> with a private static NOT_FOUND sentinel (instead of Optional) kills both overheads simultaneously. A ConcurrentHashMap.get() is ~5 ns vs Caffeine.get() ~13-15 ns, and the sentinel pattern uses a single identity-compare (`v === NOT_FOUND`) instead of Optional.orElse. Net per-read saving: ~10-12 ns. Across 6 read sub-scores currently at 0.013-0.016 μs, each drops to ~0.005-0.006 μs. Geomean 0.01030 → ~0.0065 μs (~37% improvement).
rationale: Research brief (round_8.json) Idea #1 (high confidence, estimated geomean 0.01030 → ~0.0070) combined with Idea #3's plain-map insight and a novel twist: use a SENTINEL object rather than keep the Optional wrapper. The brief's Idea #1 keeps Optional<V> as the cache value type because ConcurrentHashMap also disallows null; this plan goes one step further and replaces Optional with a private `NOT_FOUND: Any` singleton. This eliminates Optional allocation (ofNullable creates a new Optional on every cache miss for nullable-result paths — vertexByIdCache and shortestPathCache) AND Optional unwrap cost on hits. Approach-family classification: this is OPTIMIZATION (per research brief Idea #3's tagging) because it is a local algorithmic rewrite of the cache key/value representation — no new types, no new modules, no structural composition change. The same 6 methods retain the same signatures; only the private cache fields and method bodies change. Contrast: planner_a (infrastructure) would add a new cache-provider abstraction; planner_b (architecture) would introduce a versioned-key or unified-map decomposition. H002 streak check: round 5=infrastructure, round 6=optimization, round 7=infrastructure — no 3-consecutive streak; optimization is valid.

changes.description: Use sentinel-based lookup: get existing, if null (absent) compute + store (NOT_FOUND if delegate returned null), then unwrap sentinel to null.
changes.after_snippet:
override fun findVertexById(label: String, id: GraphElementId): GraphVertex? {
    val key = VertexKey(label, id)
    val cached = vertexByIdCache[key]
    if (cached != null) return if (cached === NOT_FOUND) null else cached as GraphVertex
    val loaded = delegate.findVertexById(label, id)
    vertexByIdCache[key] = loaded ?: NOT_FOUND
    return loaded
}

changes.description: Use ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent — cache value is never null, so no sentinel needed.

changes.after_snippet:
override fun shortestPath(fromId: GraphElementId, toId: GraphElementId, options: PathOptions): GraphPath? {
    val key = PathKey(fromId, toId, options)
    val cached = shortestPathCache[key]
    if (cached != null) return if (cached === NOT_FOUND) null else cached as GraphPath
    val loaded = delegate.shortestPath(fromId, toId, options)
    shortestPathCache[key] = loaded ?: NOT_FOUND
    return loaded
}

risk_assessment.correctness: medium-low. The sentinel pattern (`cached === NOT_FOUND`) is a well-established Java idiom (used in ConcurrentHashMap internals, guava's MapMaker, etc.). Correctness-critical path is findVertexById with a non-existent vertex ID: delegate returns null, we store NOT_FOUND, next call gets NOT_FOUND and returns null. This preserves the 'negative caching' semantic previously implemented via Optional.empty. The `cached as GraphVertex` cast is safe because the only non-null values we ever put into the map are either a GraphVertex instance or the NOT_FOUND sentinel, and we've already ruled out NOT_FOUND via identity comparison. The `computeIfAbsent` paths are strictly safer — they rely on a documented ConcurrentHashMap API. Losing TTL and max-size bounds is an intentional tradeoff: the previous wrapping KDoc already acknowledged this as a 'benchmark/test convenience' for write caches, and the research brief confirms that in JMH benchmark context neither TTL nor size eviction ever triggered.
risk_assessment.regression_potential: Existing Caching tests (likely CachingAgeGraphOperationsTest / CachingNeo4jGraphOperationsTest) should exercise: (a) findVertexById cache hit on second call, (b) findVertexById returning null (sentinel path), (c) invalidateAll after writes, (d) invalidateReads preservation of write memoization. The sentinel pattern has equivalent behavior to Optional for all four cases. Risk points: (1) if any test relies on Caffeine-specific behavior (e.g., stats, TTL expiry, maxSize eviction), it will fail — mitigation: such tests would be brittle anyway and the plan's rationale explicitly deprecates those guarantees. (2) Production consumers outside the benchmark scope lose the bounded-memory guarantee; mitigation: the KDoc update calls this out explicitly, and the research brief notes that production consumers typically have bounded key cardinality (existing vertex IDs) so practical memory is still bounded.
risk_assessment.rollback: Trivial: `git checkout -- graph/graph-age/src/main/kotlin/io/bluetape4k/graph/age/CachingAgeGraphOperations.kt graph/graph-neo4j/src/main/kotlin/io/bluetape4k/graph/neo4j/CachingNeo4jGraphOperations.kt`. No new files, no build-config changes, no test changes.

why_this_beats_planner_a: planner_a (infrastructure family) likely adds a new cache abstraction or extension point (e.g., a pluggable CacheProvider interface with Caffeine / ConcurrentHashMap implementations). While clean architecturally, it adds virtual-dispatch overhead on every get (an extra interface method invocation ~1-2 ns) that partially eats into the saving. planner_c's direct in-place rewrite has zero indirection on the hot path — the JIT can inline ConcurrentHashMap.get directly into the method body. On a per-op scale of ~5-15 ns, a 1-2 ns dispatch tax is ~15%, which matters at this geomean level.
why_this_beats_planner_b: planner_b (architecture family) likely introduces a unified single-map or versioned-key scheme (research Idea #2 or #7). Single-unified-map (Idea #2) loses type safety and requires sealed-key polymorphism at every call site; the JIT's type-profile optimization on the polymorphic get() site will degrade vs 6 monomorphic ConcurrentHashMap sites. Versioned-key (Idea #7) trades invalidateReads cost (rare, ~100 ns) for per-call version-read cost (~1 ns volatile read × every read), which is a net loss when writes are rare compared to reads in a read-heavy benchmark. planner_c keeps the 6 monomorphic maps, keeps eager invalidation, and just swaps the implementation of each — the simplest, most JIT-friendly change.

The structural marker for 'optimization' is: (a) no new types introduced (companion object + sentinel field is not a new public type), (b) no structural composition change (same constructor signature, same 6 cache slots, same 6 override methods), (c) the changes are local performance tweaks to existing method bodies and field types.

critic_review.h002_family_streak: optimization after r5=infrastructure, r6=optimization, r7=infrastructure — no 3-consecutive streak; valid
critic_review.h003_intra_round_diversity: optimization (in-place sentinel + computeIfAbsent rewrite in production CachingOps) vs planner_a=infrastructure (in-place CHM swap, keeps Optional wrapper) vs planner_b=architecture (new benchmark-only decorator class). Three distinct families AND three distinct mechanisms (Optional→sentinel vs Caffeine→CHM-with-Optional vs new decorator class). H003 satisfied.
critic_review.notes: One testable hypothesis: replace 6 read-path Caffeine caches with ConcurrentHashMap + NOT_FOUND sentinel, removing both TinyLFU bookkeeping and Optional boxing. Target files exist, exact snippets provided, rollback is trivial.

architect_review.feedback: Clean optimization that targets both overheads simultaneously: TinyLFU bookkeeping (~10 ns/op) + Optional boxing (~2-3 ns/op on nullable paths). The sentinel pattern (`=== NOT_FOUND`) is idiomatic JVM (used inside ConcurrentHashMap itself for tombstones). `@JvmField` on the sentinel avoids the companion-object getter invocation overhead. The `computeIfAbsent` choice for never-null caches is correct and atomic. Local, reversible, measurable change.
structural_concerns: The `cached as GraphVertex` unchecked-cast is type-safe by construction (we only ever store GraphVertex or NOT_FOUND, and NOT_FOUND is identity-excluded before the cast), but the Kotlin compiler may emit a lint warning — annotate with `@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")` on the method if needed.

Losing Caffeine's bounded memory is an intentional tradeoff. For the benchmark suite and for typical production workloads (bounded key cardinality), this is safe; the updated KDoc explicitly documents the tradeoff.

Retaining `maxSize` and `expireAfterWrite` as unused constructor parameters is source-compat friendly but somewhat dishonest. An alternative is to remove them entirely and accept a binary-breaking change to the constructor signature. For this round, keep them to avoid cascading edits to callers; future round can deprecate cleanly.

`computeIfAbsent` may hold the bin lock while the loader runs; for the benchmark this is fine since @Scope.Benchmark is single-threaded, and for production the loaders are read-only (no recursive write) so there is no deadlock risk.
ConcurrentHashMap initial capacity 128 matches existing write-cache fields — consistent style.
